chapter: Fletcher Henderson and forming his own band
title: Fletcher Henderson as a giant step up
summary: Joining Henderson was a big step because the music was more challenging than Charlie Johnson's stock arrangements.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Uh huh. Then we reach what I think in perspective, and certainly what jazz historians would say was an important point -- when you went to Fletcher Henderson at some point in there. In and out, but you had an association there. You mentioned earlier that you felt very pleased because Fletcher's band had a big reputation,

and a musician was known to have arrived in some sense, at least, when he was invited to sit with that orchestra. In retrospect now, however, do you regard that as a very important turning point in your career?
Yes, I do. It was really -- it was like a giant step up.

You know? And that doesn't mean to say that the Charlie Johnson orchestra and the others were not, you know, good, or -- but they didn't -- what happened was that their music was not as challenging. That's it.
There were a lot of stock arrangements? At that time?

Yeah, a lot of stock arrangements and you know, well -- of course you've heard the things that Charlie Johnson did when I was with the band, anyway, and they -- I'm trying to remember if Edgar Sampson did any writing for them while I was with him. I'm not sure. Probably later; probably he was with them later on.
